title: Finite-type affine frames and purity-domain geometry for a vector bundle
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\mathcal E$ be a locally free $\mathcal O_S$-module of constant rank $d\geq0$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Let $\pi:V=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\operatorname{Sym}^\bullet\mathcal E)\to S$ be its vector bundle and $z:S\to V$ its augmentation zero section [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. No separatedness of $S$ over $k$ is assumed.

The schemes $S,V$ are Noetherian, and $\pi$ is affine, quasi-compact, separated and of finite type, and smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There is a finite affine open cover $S=\bigcup_i U_i$, with each $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ and $R_i$ finitely generated over $k$, and frames $\mathcal E|_{U_i}\cong\mathcal O_{U_i}^{\oplus d}$. Each frame gives a $U_i$-isomorphism $V_i=\pi^{-1}U_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_i[x_1,\ldots,x_d]=\mathbf A^d_{U_i}$ [def-sbc-affine-space], identifying $\pi$ with the polynomial projection and $z$ with the coordinate-zero section. The $V_i$ form an open cover of $V$ and are affine, separated finite-type $k$-schemes. On overlaps the restrictions of these frames can be compared on affine refinements whose coordinate rings are finitely generated over $k$; no affineness of $U_i\cap U_j$ is asserted. The assertions include the empty scheme with the empty cover and $d=0$, when $\pi$ and its zero section are the identity under the canonical rank-zero identification.

proof.text: Obtain IsNoetherian S using LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian and QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace over the Noetherian field spectrum. Choose a module frame cover by exists_restrict_iso_free. Shrink a frame neighbourhood of each point using Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens, restricting the frame by restrictCompIso and the coproduct-preserving restriction functor. Compactness supplies a finite subcover, reindexed by Fin n. If S is empty choose Fin 0 from the outset.

The definition of over already supplies IsAffineHom of the bundle projection. Thus it is quasi-compact and separated. For each module frame use trivializationMap_spec to identify the restricted projection with an affine-space projection after an isomorphism. AffineSpace.smoothOfRelativeDimension_over, invariance under isomorphisms, and target locality of SmoothOfRelativeDimension d prove smoothness of relative dimension d globally. This implies Smooth, hence local finite presentation and local finite type. Finite type over S makes the total space Noetherian.

For rank zero each restricted affine-space projection is an isomorphism because its variable type is empty. Target locality of isomorphisms proves that the bundle projection is an isomorphism. Its existing section equation zero_spec identifies its inverse with zero. Preimages of the finite frame cover cover the total space by Scheme.Hom.iSup_preimage_eq_top.

For every affine frame open, trivializationMap_spec supplies the chart isomorphism and both the projection and zero-section equations. Its composite with AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine is the required polynomial-spectrum isomorphism. Affineness of the chart implies separatedness and quasi-compactness over Spec k; local finite type follows by composition. Apply HasRingHomProperty.iff_of_isAffine and compose with the ring isomorphism Scheme.ΓSpecIso.inv to obtain finite type of the base coordinate ring over k.

Shrink a neighbourhood of each point of an overlap to an affine T using the affine-open basis. Restrict the two original frames using restrictCompIso and the free-sheaf coproduct comparison for restriction. The formula ιFree_mapFreeIso_hom and naturality of the frame morphism show that the new frame sections are exactly the restrictions of the original sections. Apply transition_spec to obtain G,H and all frame and coordinate identities. The finite-type assertion for Γ(T) is the same affine-pair argument as above. Empty matrices and sums are covered by the existing transition_spec.

Step 1: Spec k is Noetherian, so S is Noetherian by 01T6; frames come from def-amb; 01IT gives affine shrinkings; quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover; 01T2 pairs with target Spec k show each R_i is finitely generated over k. Step 2: θ_U gives A(U_i)≅Sym_{R_i}(E(U_i)); relative-spec (2),(3),(4) and 00DM give V_i≅Spec R_i[x], with z equal to the coordinate-zero section by the augmentation clause of def-asd. Step 3: π is affine by the existential cover criterion 01S8, quasi-compact and separated by 01S7, locally of finite type by the pointwise criterion, hence of finite type, and V is Noetherian by 01T6. Step 4: finite type over k by explicit generators; separated because the source is affine (01KN/01KV); separatedness of S is never used. Step 5: A^d is smooth of relative dimension d; restrict (c) and then (b) give π_i and π∘j_i smooth, and local-on-source gives π smooth; the fibre over s∈U_i lies entirely in V_i, which gives dim_x=d at every point. Step 6: affine refinements of overlaps with transition matrices as in def-asd; no affine intersections are assumed. Step 7: the empty base and d=0 hold (E=0, Sym=R, A^0_S=S). The def-asd Noetherian hypothesis is supplied by Step 1. Edge cases tested: a non-separated glued A^1 base, a nonreduced base, rank 0 and any characteristic. Duplicate check: lem-pur-line-zero-geometry is a different, stronger rank-one package with a separated base, so it is not a duplicate. The citer det-sp-orientation-vector-bundle uses only clauses proved here. The three generic tool_uses are accepted. No changes.
